title: F. Deglado
statement:
You are given a 2n × 2n grid a where each column is a permutation^{∗} of length 2n.

We want to sort all columns in ascending order from top to bottom by performing the following operation:

Choose a 2 × 2 subgrid and swap the two top elements with the two bottom elements.More formally, you can choose two integers i and j (1 ≤ i, j < 2n), then swap a_{i,j} with a_{i+1,j} and swap a_{i,j+1} with a_{i+1,j+1}.

You have to sort all columns using at most n · 2n choose 2 + 9n operations, or determine that it is impossible.

Note that you do not need to minimize the number of operations.

^{∗}A permutation of length m is an array consisting of m distinct integers from 1 to m in arbitrary order. For example, [2,3,1,5,4] is a permutation, but [1,2,2] is not a permutation (2 appears twice in the array), and [1,3,4] is also not a permutation (m=3 but there is 4 in the array).

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 500). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 80).

The i-th line of the next 2n lines contains 2n integers a_{i,1},a_{i,2},…,a_{i,2n} (1 ≤ a_{i,j} ≤ 2n) — the elements of the i-th row of the grid.

It is guaranteed that every column in the grid forms a permutation of length 2n.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n^3 over all test cases does not exceed 80^3.

For each test case, if it is impossible to sort all columns in at most n · 2n choose 2 + 9n operations, print -1 in a single line.

Otherwise, in the first line print a single integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ n · 2n choose 2 + 9n) — the number of operations.

Then k lines follow, the w-th line containing two integers i_w and j_w (1 ≤ i_w, j_w < 2n) — you choose i_w and j_w in the w-th operation.

In the first test case, you can sort columns using one operation.

In the second test case, it can be shown that you cannot sort columns.

The illustration of the third test case:

Input:
```
3
1
2 2
1 1
1
1 2
2 1
2
1 2 2 1
2 1 3 3
4 4 1 2
3 3 4 4
```

Output:
```
1
1 1
-1
3
3 1
2 3
1 2
```
